subject: A-Level Business
question: 'Limited liability is only of benefit to the shareholders of a business.' Do you agree? Justify your view.

mark_scheme.instruction: Levels of response. Determine the level using the descriptors (best fit), then the mark within the level. Indicative content is not exhaustive - credit all valid lines of argument.
demands: analysing its effects on shareholders AND other stakeholders
judging whether the benefits are confined to shareholders
indicative_content: shareholders' personal assets are protected, so they only lose the value of their investment
it encourages investment, so shareholders can diversify portfolios
creditors (suppliers, banks) may lose out if a company fails because they cannot claim owners' personal assets
limited liability encourages investment and enterprise, creating jobs (employees) and products (customers)
it allows large plcs to raise capital, financing growth that benefits the economy and government (tax)
suppliers and banks can protect themselves with credit checks, security or credit limits
the separation of ownership and control may benefit managers

subject: A-Level Business
scenario:
PureBloom Cosmetics plc makes vegan, cruelty-free skincare products sold through UK supermarkets, its own website and 30 PureBloom stores. Its mission is 'beauty that does no harm'. Its products are priced about 20% above mass-market brands.

In January 2024 an environmental campaign group, ClearSeas, criticised PureBloom for packaging most products in single-use plastic. ClearSeas posted its findings on social media and they were widely shared. PureBloom's share price fell from 412p to 371p in the following week.

PureBloom's directors are considering switching to refillable aluminium packaging. This would add an estimated 18p to the cost of each product and would require a £4m investment in new filling equipment.
question: Explain why PureBloom's share price fell after the ClearSeas criticism.

mark_scheme.instruction: Levels of response. Determine the level using the descriptors (best fit), then the mark within the level. Indicative content is not exhaustive - credit all valid lines of argument.
indicative_content: investors expected the criticism to damage PureBloom's reputation with ethically aware customers, reducing future sales and profits
PureBloom's brand is built on 'beauty that does no harm', so the criticism undermines its USP and premium pricing
the cost of changing packaging (18p per product and £4m) would reduce future profits/dividends
more investors wanted to sell than buy, so the price fell by 10% (412p to 371p)

subject: A-Level Business
topic: 3.1.1 Understanding the nature and purpose of business
scenario:
Background
Tom and Ama Mensah set up GreenRoot Organics Ltd in 2012 on a 120-acre farm in Herefordshire. GreenRoot grows organic vegetables and delivers weekly vegetable boxes to 4 200 subscribers in the West Midlands. Its mission is 'Good food, fairly grown'.

GreenRoot employs 46 people, including 12 adults with learning disabilities who work in its packing shed through a supported-employment scheme. Staff are paid at least the Real Living Wage. Tom and Ama reinvest about 80% of profits in the farm and the local community.

A supermarket contract
A regional supermarket chain has offered GreenRoot a one-year contract to supply 200 tonnes of organic carrots and potatoes. The supermarket would pay 60 days after delivery. GreenRoot's spare land could produce only 150 tonnes; the remaining 50 tonnes would have to come from land currently used to grow vegetables for the boxes.

Growth options
Tom and Ama want GreenRoot to grow so that it can employ more people from the supported-employment scheme. They are considering two options.

Option 1: open three GreenRoot farm shops in nearby towns. This would be financed by raising £600 000 through crowd funding, offering investors 6% interest a year for five years.

Option 2: franchise the GreenRoot veg-box model to other organic farms across the UK. Each franchisee would pay a £20 000 fee and 6% of revenue, and would have to follow GreenRoot's employment and sourcing standards.
